<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Papua conflict]]
**Tensions escalate between [[Indonesia]] and Pacific Island nations as the situation in the province of [[West Papua (province)|West Papua]] worsens after an [[Indonesian National Armed Forces|Indonesian soldier]] and a West Papuan are killed in clashes. [[Vanuatu|Vanuatuan]] Foreign Minister [[Ralph Regenvanu]] said "something must be done", amid calls to invite United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights [[Michelle Bachelet]] to investigate murders and torture in the area. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/397733/surge-in-papua-violence-prompts-stronger-stand-from-pacific-leaders (Radio New Zealand)] 
*[[Hamas]] says it has captured an [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] cell responsible for Tuesday's suicide bombings that killed three policemen. Hamas says ten are in custody. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/hamas-says-it-captured-cell-behind-gaza-suicide-bombings-that-killed-cops/ (''The Times of Israel'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2019 Amazon rainforest wildfires]]
**[[Brazil]] bans [[deforestation in Brazil|land clearance fires]] for 60 days in response to the ongoing disaster. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-49507405 (BBC News)]
*At least seven spectators have died after a flash flood swept across the pitch at a local match in the village of Tizert, [[Morocco]]. [https://news.sky.com/story/seven-die-as-floodwater-hits-local-football-match-in-morocco-11797224 (Sky News)]
*The number of people killed in the collapse of an apartment building yesterday in western [[Ukraine]] rose to eight, including one child. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-ukraine-incident/death-toll-in-ukraine-building-collapse-rises-to-eight-emergency-services-idUSKCN1VJ0CQ (Reuters)]
*[[USS Fitzgerald and MV ACX Crystal collision|USS ''Fitzgerald'' and MV ''ACX Crystal'' collision]]
**The [[Japan Transport Safety Board]] concludes its investigation into a fatal collision between [[USS Fitzgerald|USS ''Fitzgerald'']] and [[Philippines|Filipino]] container ship ''ACX Crystal''. The board's final report concludes distraction and incomplete radar information aboard the [[US Navy]] vessel caused the accident. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2019/08/29/national/japan-report-us-destroyer-collision (''The Japan Times'')]
*The volcano on the [[Italy|Italian]] island of [[Stromboli]] erupts, an event described as "high intensity" by the [[National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/stromboli-volcano-eruption-italy-island-tourist-a9083161.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[2019 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] [[Governor of Georgia|Governor]] [[Brian Kemp]] declares a [[state of emergency]] for several counties in anticipation of [[Hurricane Dorian]], which is expected to make landfall in the upcoming days. [https://www.news4jax.com/news/georgia/help-available-for-disabled-georgians-in-case-of-a-hurricane (WJXT)]

;Health and environment
*[[Ethiopia]] plants 350 million trees in 12 hours, breaking the previous world record held by [[India]] since 2016 of 50 million trees planted in the same time. [https://www.unenvironment.org/news-and-stories/story/ethiopia-plants-over-350-million-trees-day-setting-new-world-record (United Nations Environment Programme)] [https://pmo.gov.et/greenlegacy/ (Office of the Prime Minister of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia)]

;International relations
*[[China–United States trade war]], [[China–United States relations]]
**China announces that it will not immediately retaliate on the latest U.S. import tariffs, but is instead "lodging solemn representations". [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2019-08-29/china-indicates-it-won-t-retaliate-against-newest-u-s-tariffs (Bloomberg)]
*The U.S. officially reestablishes [[United States Space Command|Space Command]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/president-donald-trump-reestablishes-us-space-command/story?id=65271426 (ABC)]
*[[Status of Jerusalem]], [[Status of territories occupied by Israel in 1967#East Jerusalem|Status of East Jerusalem]]
**[[Israel]] announces that, on 16 August, [[Nauru]] officially recognized [[Jerusalem]] as the [[capital of Israel]]. [https://www.jns.org/republic-of-nauru-recognizes-jerusalem-as-israels-capital/ (Jewish News Syndicate)]
**The [[Foreign Affairs Minister of the Palestinian National Authority]] announces that it will file a complaint to the [[United Nations]] after [[Honduras]]' recognition of the disputed city of Jerusalem as the capital of Israel. [[Palestinians]] see [[East Jerusalem]] as the capital of the future [[State of Palestine]]. [https://www.dailystar.com.lb/News/Middle-East/2019/Aug-29/490665-palestinians-to-file-complaint-over-honduras-jerusalem-move.ashx (AFP via ''The Daily Star'')]

;Law and crime
*[[Capital punishment in Thailand]] 
**The [[Supreme Court of Thailand]] upholds death sentences against two migrant workers convicted of murdering two [[United Kingdom|UK]] tourists and [[rape|raping]] one. Rights groups say that the men are scapegoats and tortured into false confessions by police under pressure to solve the crimes, which attracted international attention. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/aug/29/death-sentences-upheld-in-thai-backpacker-case-zaw-lin-wai-phyo-hannah-witheridge-david-miller (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2019 Hong Kong anti-extradition bill protests]]
**[[Hong Kong]] police ban a planned Saturday march by the [[Civil Human Rights Front]], saying there is "a high chance that certain violent protesters will hijack this event". The CHRF plans to appeal. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2019-08-29/hong-kong-police-will-ban-mass-weekend-protest-march-scmp-says (Bloomberg)]
*The [[Office of Inspector General]] of the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]] releases its final report in which former director [[James Comey]] is criticised for his leaking of documents regarding [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]]. However, it does not recommend he be prosecuted. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-49513403 (BBC News)]
*[[Rotherham child sexual exploitation scandal]]
**Six [[Pakistanis in England|Pakistani]] men are found guilty of abusing and raping teenage girls between 1998 and 2002 in [[Rotherham]], [[England]]. The [[National Crime Agency]] believes as many as 1,510 teenagers were sexually exploited in the town during the same period. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-south-yorkshire-49500387 (BBC News)]
*[[Identitarian movement]]
**A [[Judiciary of France|French court]] jails several members of [[Les Identitaires|Generation Identity]] and fines the organisation over an anti-immigration operation in the [[Alps]]. They were found guilty of "exercising activities in conditions that could create confusion with a public function". The case was that the operation could be mistaken for a government action. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/far-right-generation-identity-members-jailed-alps-france-asylum-seekers-a9084976.html (''The Independent'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Politics of Italy]]
**[[President of Italy]] [[Sergio Mattarella]] tasks demissionary [[Prime Minister of Italy|Prime Minister]] [[Giuseppe Conte]] with the formation of a new [[Council of Ministers (Italy)|cabinet]], a [[coalition government|coalition]] of [[Five Star Movement]] and [[Democratic Party (Italy)|Democratic Party]]. The premier-designate reserves the right to accept the mandate, pending further talks with both parties. [http://www.ansa.it/english/news/politics/2019/08/29/mattarella-gives-conte-mandate_de5c7f54-978c-4ac7-88e8-bae156d12cba.html (ANSA)]
*[[Politics of Ukraine]]
**[[Oleksiy Honcharuk]] becomes the new [[Prime Minister of Ukraine]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/08/oleksiy-honcharuk-ukraine-prime-minister-190829160052863.html (Al Jazeera)] 
*[[Politics of the United Kingdom]], [[Brexit]]
**The [[Court of Session]] in [[Edinburgh]] begins hearing arguments in a case challenging [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|UK Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]]'s decision to suspend the [[Parliament of the United Kingdom|UK Parliament]]. The challenge, seeking an interdict, the [[Scots law|Scottish equivalent]] to an [[injunction]], to prevent the move, is being brought by [[Member of the Scottish Parliament|Members]] of the [[Scottish Parliament]]. The judge announces he will consider his position overnight and give his judgement tomorrow at 10:00 local time. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-scotland-politics-49509712 (BBC News)]
**[[Ruth Davidson]] steps down as leader of the [[Scottish Conservatives]]. She has been a critic of Johnson, himself a [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative]], especially his approach to Brexit. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-scotland-politics-49509275 (BBC News)]

;Science and technology
*An [[Iranian Space Agency]] [[Simorgh (rocket)|Simorgh]] [[Launch vehicle|carrier rocket ]] explodes on the launch pad at [[Imam Khomeini Spaceport]] in southeastern [[Iran]]. This is Iran's third failed attempt to reach orbit this year following launches in January and February. [https://www.npr.org/2019/08/29/755406765/iranian-rocket-launch-ends-in-failure-images-show (NPR)]
